az_camelback_mountain.blurb: Camelback Mountain stands inside the Phoenix metro area, between the Arcadia neighborhood and Paradise Valley, and is described as the closest climbing to Phoenix. It holds a mix of sport and trad, with some bouldering and a little aid, and grades from easy up to 5.12 that concentrate between 5.7 and 5.10. The rock changes across the mountain: the east side, Camel's Hump, is granite, while the west side, Camel's Head, is sedimentary, and the Praying Monk is a red sandstone formation. Gargoyle Wall holds the most climbs, followed by the Western Bouldering Area, The Headwall, Bobby's Rock and The Praying Monk.

bc_cariboo.blurb: Cariboo gathers climbing across British Columbia's Cariboo country, led by Marble Canyon and Williams Lake's Esler Bluffs. Sport is the most common style, followed by trad, with mixed climbs, ice and a few top-rope routes. Rock grades are mostly 5.7 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, and the ice and mixed climbs reach WI5 and M8. Marble Canyon, in the Pavilion Mountain Range of south-central British Columbia, holds the most climbs: a limestone canyon over 800 meters high, with rock quality that ranges from bullet-proof grey to rotten red, mostly moderate multi-pitch lines, and a climate that is arid and sunny most of the year. Esler Bluffs, near Williams Lake, has north- and south-facing walls, mostly sport, with most bolted routes on the north-facing walls. Bridge River Valley is mostly ice.

bc_grohman_narrows.blurb: Grohman Narrows is a granite bouldering area near Nelson in the Kootenays of British Columbia, set along the highway toward Castlegar beside the railway tracks and the river. Everything here is bouldering, with plenty of problems from easy through V5 and a thinner run of harder ones up to the V9 range. The stone is fine-grained and textured, with lines following lips, cracks and arêtes, and slopers, smeary feet and committing top-outs are the norm. Hippy, Tree Fort, Track and Cave hold the most problems. Most of the bouldering is shaded. Spring is often sunny and mild, July to September runs hot, fall is good for sending, and snow arrives from about November to late March.

bc_slocan_valley.blurb: The Slocan Valley runs about 100 km through the West Kootenay of southeastern British Columbia, with Slocan Lake at its northern end, the Valhalla Range along its steep western side and the Slocan River to the south. Sport and trad make up most of the climbing, along with some bouldering and alpine routes, and grades concentrate between 5.9 and 5.11. Slocan Lake Bluffs, near the town of Slocan on the lake's east side, run about a kilometer along an old road beside the water, with sport climbs whose classics span 5.6 to 5.11a. The Valhalla Mountains are a different world: gneiss with horizontal black bands, big-wall, trad and alpine climbing, and Mount Gimli among the peaks, with access following snowmelt. Helheim and Poison River Bluffs are other areas in the valley.

ca_big_rock_area.blurb: Big Rock Area sits in the southern part of Lake Perris State Recreation Area in Riverside County, California. Its centerpiece, Big Rock itself, is a giant granite rock about 180 feet high, whose west face is shaded in the morning and catches lots of afternoon sun. The climbing is low-angled slab with generous bolted protection, suited to beginners and novices, and most routes can be done in a single pitch. There is also some bouldering around the base and on the surrounding hillsides. Main Slab holds the most climbs, followed by Bernasconi Ridge and L-Slab/Lakeview Slab. Grades are mostly easy to moderate, with a smaller number of harder climbs.
